# canary edge tests · COLUMNS=80 · colour off
Forward tests
  A forward test is a rule written down before the decisions it is read on: only
  decisions made after the rule was registered count. Canary counts them; the
  reading that turns a full count into an answer is not built yet. In the rules
  about sales, a sale a protection rule sent is read apart from one you chose; a
  stop placed directly at the broker cannot be told apart yet.

  Nothing is counted in this reply: the daemon has no decision review yet, the
  rules are not registered yet, or the daemon runs a build that does not count.
  The rules and their read points are below.

Not counted in this reply  7 rules

  Are your stock sales followed by weaker prices than a sale a few days later
  would have been?
    informs selling · nothing to check first: every decision counts
    read at 80 · counts one name in one week with a stock or ETF sale

  Do your entries do better than the same entry on a random nearby day?
    informs buying · nothing to check first: every decision counts
    read at 167 · counts one name in one week with an entry

  Do option buys made while premium at risk was at or below the budget line pay
  better than buys made above it?
    informs buying · checks premium at risk at the last statement against the
      Rulebook's premium budget line
    read at 30 · counts one contract in one week, final when its position has
      closed

  Do single-name option buys made the session after a Regime warning do better
  or worse than the rest?
    informs buying · checks Regime's stage at the last close
    read at 40 · counts one contract in one week, final when its position has
      closed

  After you close an option position, is the contract worth more or less five
  sessions later?
    informs holding or selling · checks the sale price against the position's
      average cost
    read at 30 · counts one closed single-name option position

  After a partial sale, would a floor at that sale's price have protected what
  was left?
    informs selling · checks the remainder's statement value against the price
      of the last partial sale
    read at 40 · counts one single-name option position with a partial sale

  Do you sell options too early after the underlying moved against you?
    informs holding or selling · checks the underlying's move over the last
      five sessions, in expected moves
    read at 50 · counts one name in one week with an option sale

Details: canary edge tests <rule> · canary edge tests --all · --json
